correctness.rationale: A length increment by one cyclic period adds phase-independent letter and adjacent-pair counts. In the remaining range \(1\le r\le a+b\), every factor has at most two transitions. The six possible run-shape types yield exactly the two constants, twice the allowable one-transition interval count, and one class for each of the two-transition shapes. Distinctness follows from first/last letters recovered from digrams and from distinct run-length digram counts; these give the exact formula. A case split in m=min(a,b), M=max(a,b) proves the maximum \(\min\{a+b,2m+2\}\), and the phase-identifiability criterion follows from equality with the number of starting phases. The standalone checker directly passed 6664 length profiles and 196 maxima/threshold cases, but finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete two-parameter classification of 2-Abelian factor complexity for a simplest nonconstant periodic family. It quantifies when bigram statistics recover every cyclic phase and gives a sharp difference-two boundary, with an explicit saturation at \(2\min(a,b)+2\) despite arbitrarily increasing total period. This is a structural and interpretable loss-of-information phenomenon, not an arbitrary finite lookup or mere reformulation of known general periodicity.
